name: Act of June 22, 1874: payment to the L'Anse and Vieux Desert Chippewa for land east of Huron Bay
aka: L'Anse reserve, T. 51 N., R. 31 W., compensation
nations: Lac Vieux Desert Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians
promises: Congress appropriated money to pay the L'Anse and Vieux Desert bands for the part of township 51 north, range 31 west, lying east of Huron Bay, which was not in the reservation the treaty of September 30, 1854 provided.
today: Royce explains that an executive order of March 7, 1855 withdrew the whole township from market instead of only the part west of Huron Bay that the 1854 treaty reserved; the eastern part was later relinquished, the Indians claimed compensation for it, and this Act granted it. No finding that a promise was broken was found for this record.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 874
Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 794

openQuestions: The Act itself (18 Stat. 140 per Royce) was not opened; govinfo did not serve that page. The amount appropriated is not recorded.
The Keweenaw Bay Indian Community's own account of the L'Anse reservation was not looked up in this pass.
